method: Read ActiveCampaign's pricing page (Email tab, the default active tab) in a US-locale headless browser at its default 1,000-contact selection, then set the page's native contacts <select> element to 10,000 and to 50,000 (a real dropdown, not a slider, so clicking the visible tier numbers does not change the selection; Playwright's selectOption was used instead) to capture Starter/Plus/Pro/Enterprise pricing at all three required contact tiers; also expanded both collapsed pricing-page FAQ answers, and read the Help Center's plan-overview, SMS add-on and billing-cadence articles plus the onboarding-services page's cost FAQ. Snapshots saved for every page/state.

freeTier.summary: No permanent free plan. ActiveCampaign offers only the 14-day free trial; none of the pricing page, the plan-overview Help Center article, or the onboarding page mention a free-forever tier.

trial.summary: 14-day free trial, no credit card required ('Free 14-day trial with email sign-up ... No credit card needed. Instant setup.' on the pricing page). The Help Center's plan-overview article adds that trial accounts run on the Professional (Pro) plan's features, and that the Sales Engagement add-on and Salesforce integration can also be tried.

extraCosts.label: Setup / onboarding fee
extraCosts.note: Pricing-page FAQ: 'There are no setup costs or hidden fees when you start with ActiveCampaign.' The onboarding-services page FAQ adds: 'Onboarding is included free with all paid ActiveCampaign plans. Depending on your plan, it may be through a live, 1:1 session or through an AI course.'

billingNotes: The public pricing page shows only the annual-billing, monthly-equivalent rate ('Billed annually') for every plan and contact tier, with no visible monthly/annual toggle. The Help Center's billing-information article confirms three billing cadences exist in-account — Annual, Monthly, and 'Commit annually pay monthly' — but does not publish the Monthly-cadence rate, and it was not found anywhere on the public marketing site (see unverified).

Contacts are sold in named bands (1,000 / 2,500 / 5,000 / 7,500 / 10,000 / 15,000 / 20,000 / 25,000 / 30,000 / 40,000 / 50,000 / >50,000). The Starter plan has a maximum of 25,000 contacts and is shown as unavailable ('Only available on plans with 25,000 contacts or less') at higher bands — confirmed both on the pricing page and in the Help Center's plan-overview article.
If a contact count grows past the current plan's contact band, ActiveCampaign upgrades the account to the next band/plan rather than penalizing or locking it out (pricing-page FAQ).

Each plan includes a fixed number of user seats (Starter 1, Plus 1, Pro 3, Enterprise 5). Starter can add at most 1 extra seat; Plus, Pro and Enterprise can buy additional seats with no stated cap — but no seat add-on price is published anywhere on activecampaign.com or its Help Center (see unverified).
A 30-day money-back guarantee applies to paid plans ('We're so confident you'll grow with us, we'll give you a full refund if you're not satisfied after 30 days' — pricing page).
The pricing page includes a Currency selector (USD $, BRL R$, CAD $, AUD A$, EUR €, GBP £); this record captures only the default USD selection.

regional.note: The pricing page offers a Currency selector (USD, BRL, CAD, AUD, EUR, GBP). We captured only the default USD selection, per this site’s US-list-price convention, and did not test whether the other currencies are simple FX conversions of the USD price or independently set regional prices.

scenarios.label: Solo operator, 1,000 contacts
scenarios.assumptions: One person managing email marketing for about 1,000 contacts and roughly 4 campaigns/month, on the cheapest plan that covers this contact count. The pricing page shows only annual billing; no month-to-month rate is published (see unverified).
scenarios.note: Starter is capped at 1 user seat and 5 actions per automation, which is enough for a solo operator at this scale.

scenarios.label: Small team, 10,000 contacts
scenarios.assumptions: About 10,000 contacts and roughly 8 campaigns/month. Starter’s 25,000-contact ceiling and feature set still cover this; billed annually (no monthly rate published).
scenarios.note: Starter still allows only 1 user seat (2 with a purchased extra seat, price unpublished) and 5 actions per automation; a team wanting more seats or richer automation would need Plus ($189/month at this contact count) or higher.

scenarios.label: Growing team, 50,000 contacts
scenarios.assumptions: About 50,000 contacts and roughly 12 campaigns/month. Starter is not sold above 25,000 contacts, so Plus is the cheapest plan that covers 50,000 contacts; billed annually (no monthly rate published).
scenarios.note: ActiveCampaign's comparison table lists an 'email sends' allowance of 10x the contact count for Plus (500,000/month). 12 campaigns to the full 50,000-contact list is 600,000 sends/month, above that figure and at Pro's 12x allowance (600,000, $969/month). We could not confirm whether that multiplier is an enforced send cap or a looser guideline (see unverified); Plus is recorded here as the cheapest plan matching the contact-capacity requirement, but Pro may be the safer real-world pick if the send allowance is a hard limit.

unverified: Month-to-month (non-annual) billing rate for any plan or contact tier: the public pricing page shows only the annual-billing monthly-equivalent price. The Help Center's billing-information article confirms 'Monthly' is one of three billing cadences available in-account (the others being Annual and 'Commit annually pay monthly'), but no Monthly-cadence rate is published on the marketing site, so it could not be captured.

Price of an extra/additional user seat beyond each plan's included seats (Starter can add 1 extra seat; Plus, Pro and Enterprise can add more) — the Help Center confirms the ability to purchase seats but never states a price; it only appears inside the billing/upgrade flow after signing up.

Enhanced CRM add-ons — Pipelines and Sales Engagement (available on Plus, Professional and Enterprise) — have no published price on activecampaign.com or its Help Center. Third-party review sites cite roughly $68/month and $111/month respectively, but those figures could not be confirmed on an ActiveCampaign-owned page, so they are not included.

SMS add-on and SMS-credit pricing: the Help Center's 'Purchase the SMS add-on' article confirms Plus, Pro and Enterprise accounts can buy SMS credits, but the cost is shown only inside an in-app purchase modal after logging in; no per-credit or per-message rate is published on any page we could read.

Custom Reports add-on price (sold separately on Plus and Professional; included free with Enterprise) and Transactional Email add-on price (available on all four plans, built on Postmark) — both are listed as purchasable in the Help Center's plan-overview article with no price shown anywhere public.

Exact meaning and enforcement of each plan's 'Email sends: Nx contact limit' figure (Starter/Plus 10x, Pro 12x, Enterprise 15x) shown in the pricing page's comparison table — it is never explained whether this is a hard monthly send cap, a fair-use guideline, or a maximum list size. See the growing scenario's note for why this matters.

Whether the other five display currencies the pricing page offers (BRL, CAD, AUD, EUR, GBP) are simple FX conversions of the USD price or independently set regional prices; only the default USD selection was captured.

ActiveCampaign HQ (a separate franchise-specific product) is reported by third parties to carry a one-time fee around $4,500; this is a different product line from the four Email plans in this record and was not verified on an ActiveCampaign-owned page, so it is not included.
